Article Title: Anti-dam agitation intensifies, spreads to Arunachal capital; cops seek to search homes of 4 protesters
Article Text:
Anti-dam protests spread in Arunachal as police seek warrants against four protesters.

GUWAHATI: The standoff over Arunachal Pradesh’s proposed 11,200MW Siang dam intensified Thursday, with police seeking search warrants against four people, including a senior journalist and an advocate, over violence in Pasighat, and protesters in state capital Itanagar demanding the release of 27 arrested youths and cancellation of the project survey.Police have sought court warrants to search homes of Tongam Rina, Tatul Jerang, Tajong Talom and Sunny Tayeng — all residents of Pasighat — over alleged arson, looting and vandalism during anti-dam protests in and around the town on Oct 23.Police told the East Siang chief judicial magistrate that clothes worn during the violence, mobile phones, digital devices and other evidence could be found at their homes. Recovery was essential to reconstruct events, the investigating officer said.In Itanagar, hundreds of youths and students rallied, demanding cancellation of the pre-feasibility survey for the proposed Siang river project. They accused govt of undermining its assurance that no dam would be built without public consent by deploying CAPF and police personnel across the Siang basin.Activist Sol Dodum said the Adi community was fighting for its land and identity. “You cannot take away the land of scheduled tribes against their will and expect them to remain silent.”
Article Summary: Arunachal Pradesh's proposed 11,200MW Siang dam has sparked anti-dam protests. Police seek warrants against four people, including a senior journalist and an advocate, over violence in Pasighat. Protesters in state capital Itanagar demanding the release of 27 arrested youths and cancellation of the project survey.

Article Title: Surrender before December 1: Supreme Court cancels bail of expelled JD(U) leader Anant Singh in Dularchand Yadav murder case
Article Text:
Anant Singh

Murder case and legal proceedings

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday cancelled the bail granted to expelled JD(U) MLA Anant Singh in the murder case of Dularchand Yadav and directed him to surrender before the authorities on or before December 1, 2026.A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and PV Varale observed that the Patna High Court had erred in granting Singh bail without adequately considering the nature of the offence and his criminal antecedents. The top court suspended the High Court's order and cancelled the relief granted to Singh.The verdict comes days after the ruling Janata Dal (United) expelled Singh and his wife, former MLA Neelam Devi, from the party for six years over alleged anti-party activities.Singh had openly defied the party leadership by campaigning for Jan Suraaj candidate Anuj Kumar Singh instead of the JD(U)'s official nominee, Neeraj Kumar, in the Patna Graduates' constituency Legislative Council elections. He also reportedly made remarks against senior party leaders and questioned the functioning of the party leadership.Following the expulsion, the Bihar government stripped Neelam Devi of her position on the State-Level Programme Implementation Committee, withdrawing her minister of state rank and entitlement to an official bungalow.On October 26, the state government's Building Construction Department issued an eviction notice directing her to vacate her official residence at 1, Mall Road in Patna.The JD(U) has also approached Bihar Assembly Speaker Prem Kumar seeking Singh's disqualification under the anti-defection law. The petition was filed under the direction of party state president Umesh Singh Kushwaha.Dularchand Yadav, a regional strongman, was murdered on October 30, 2025, during a clash in Mokama Tal while campaigning for the Bihar Assembly elections was underway. Yadav was backing Jan Suraaj candidate Piyush Priyadarshi when his supporters allegedly clashed with Singh's convoy.According to the FIR registered at Ghoswari police station, Singh and his aides allegedly dragged Yadav out of his vehicle, shot him in the leg, assaulted him and ran over him with an SUV.Singh, however, claimed that the incident was part of a political conspiracy orchestrated by a rival politician. He alleged that Jan Suraaj supporters had attacked his convoy first.Bihar Police arrested Singh on November 1, 2025, and lodged him in Beur Central Jail. Despite being in custody, he contested and won the Mokama Assembly seat on a JD(U) ticket.The Patna high court granted him bail on March 19, 2026, following which he was released from prison. The bail order was subsequently challenged in the Supreme Court in October by Neeraj Kumar, the grandson of Dularchand Yadav.
Article Summary: Supreme Court cancels bail granted to expelled JD(U) MLA Anant Singh in the murder case of Dularchand Yadav. Justices MM Sundresh and PV Varale observed that the Patna High Court had erred in granting Singh bail without adequately considering the nature of the offence and his criminal antecedents.

Article Title: Opposition may gather 15,000 people but ballot will decide fate of government: BJP
Article Text:
File photo: Union minitister Kiren Rijiju

NEW DELHI: BJP is banking on twin planks of combativeness and persuasion directed at the opposition and the masses, respectively, as it looks to step up its nationwide mobilisation of people in the coming days, with top organisational functionaries and Union ministers Thursday giving shape to the party’s strategy ahead of INDIA bloc’s rally on Nov 1.“If they (opposition), for the sake of showing power, can gather 15,000 people at one place, we can gather much bigger crowds in many places the same day. But this cannot decide the fate of govt as it is for voters to do through ballot boxes,” Union minister Kiren Rijiju said after attending the BJP meeting chaired by its president Nitin Nabin.Ministers Shivraj Singh Chouhan, Piyush Goyal and Ashwini Vaishnaw; ex-minister Dharmendra Pradhan; and party members were present in the day-long meeting to finalise upcoming programmes.Party members were given literature carrying details of SIR of electoral rolls, a move aimed at disseminating the “facts” of the contentious exercise slammed by Congress, its allies and some activist groups as Election Commission’s bid to favour the governing alliance and denting the opposition.Nabin expressed confidence that BJP’s rivals will bite the dust. “BJP’s ideology has found so much acceptance that even those who do not vote for it acknowledge that only PM can lead the nation in the right direction,” he said.While BJP has zeroed in on seven outreach modes, including press conferences and interactions involving eminent citizens and the youth in nearly 800 places across country, mobilisation of a large number of people through “padyatra” (foot marches) in cities is its key instrument to blunt the opposition’s move to raise the heat on Election Commission and govt through its similar measures and rallies.
Article Summary: BJP is banking on twin planks of combativeness and persuasion directed at the opposition and the masses. Top organisational functionaries and Union ministers are giving shape to the party’s strategy ahead of INDIA bloc's rally on Nov 1. Party members were given literature carrying details of SIR of electoral rolls.

NEW DELHi: Trinamool Congress (TMC) national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee on Thursday warned police officers allegedly targeting party workers to please West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari. He added that those responsible would face consequences when his party returned to power.“I am keeping a list of names. None will be spared once the government changes,” Banerjee said, accusing police officers of implicating thousands of TMC workers in false cases at the behest of the chief minister.“I will identify the names of the police officers who are acting at his (Adhikari's) behest. I will record their names. Those who are trying to please the chief minister and secure good postings will see the consequences in two years,” he said.Banerjee alleged that several police officers had been targeting TMC workers to secure favourable postings and warned that their actions would be scrutinised if the party returned to power. He also accused an IPS officer in Paschim Medinipur of targeting TMC workers despite having earlier congratulated him on the party's expected electoral victory.The remarks come amid a political confrontation between the ruling BJP and the TMC following the arrest of former West Bengal minister Indranil Sen over alleged financial irregularities linked to Durga Puja preview shows and the sale of passes.Adhikari has alleged that Sen may not have been the sole beneficiary of the suspected irregularities, claiming that the investigation could reach more prominent political figures, including former chief minister Mamata Banerjee. He has maintained that the law would take its course regardless of the influence of those under investigation.Hitting back at the BJP over Sen's arrest, Abhishek Banerjee alleged that people who refused to compromise their conscience were being jailed, while those accused of serious offences were spared after joining the saffron party.The case centres on alleged irregularities involving MassArt Society, which investigators suspect collected money between 2022 and 2025 through passes for privileged entry to Durga Puja pandals and preview shows while creating a false impression of an association with UNESCO. The organisation's financial transactions and the use of the funds collected are under investigation.
Article Summary: Abhishek Banerjee warns police officers allegedly targeting party workers to please West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari. Article Title: Introspect on Varanasi, Nagpur losses, Congress tells BJP
Article Text:
File photo: Congress leader Jairam Ramesh

NEW DELHI: A day after PM Narendra Modi’s sarcastic remark questioning the seats won by Congress in MLC polls, the party shot back that the PM should introspect why BJP lost in his constituency Varanasi, RSS headquarters of Nagpur, and other places.Congress spokesperson Jairam Ramesh said the MLC polls — in Varanasi, Nagpur, Lucknow, Prayagraj, and Patna — are a vote of no-confidence on Modi govt’s policies. Congress Maharashtra in-charge, Sirivella Prasad, said MVA won three of the five seats in the state, and the victory of Congress candidate in BJP stronghold of Nagpur “sends a strong message”.Ramesh said, “PM needs to introspect, but instead, he’s sermonising others. Before counting Congress’s seats, I wish he would also reflect on why BJP lost both seats in his own parliamentary constituency of Varanasi, and how Congress managed to defeat BJP in RSS’s stronghold of Nagpur?”Party chief Mallikarjun Kharge challenged Modi to dissolve Parliament and hold elections on ballot papers.
Article Summary: Congress spokesperson Jairam Ramesh said the MLC polls are a vote of no- confidence on Modi govt’s policies. Congress Maharashtra in-charge, Sirivella Prasad, said MVA won three of the five seats in the state.

Article Title: 'Ballot paper, still we ask': Kharge dares BJP to dissolve Parliament after MLC poll setback
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Thursday reiterated the opposition's demand for voting using ballot paper despite the party's lacklustre performance in the Karnataka MLC elections, which were held using ballot papers.Reacting to the Karnataka MLC results, Kharge said the opposition would not give up its demand for ballot paper voting simply because BJP won the elections. He also challenged the BJP to dissolve Parliament and contest elections using ballot papers."Ballot paper, still we ask. It doesn't mean that we should leave because they are winning. Once upon a time they won only two Parliament seats. Sometimes it happens, that doesn't mean that party has no hold," Kharge said."That ego should not be there in BJP that they have done very well. If that is the case, let them dissolve the Parliament and go on ballot paper," he added.Kharge's remarks came after Prime Minister Narendra Modi took a dig at Congress for "drawing a blank" in recent MLC elections. The grand old party had won zero seats till Wednesday night. The party, however, opened its account after retaining Nagpur Division Graduates' constituency seat."MLC elections in 28 seats across 4 big states - Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Bihar and Karnataka. Elections held using ballot papers. Guess how many seats Congress won?" PM Modi said in a post on X.BJP national president Nitin Nabin also targeted Congress, saying the party would continue to struggle for survival under Rahul Gandhi's leadership. Addressing a gathering during the BJP's ‘Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao’ march in Delhi, Nabin said PM Narendra Modi would return to the Red Fort after the 2029 Lok Sabha elections.Nabin also accused Congress of opposing the revision of electoral rolls because it was distressed by efforts to remove alleged infiltrators.“There are voters who have died but whose names remain on the electoral rolls. There are also people whose names appear in the voter lists at two places. There are crores of such voters whose names are registered more than once, while the whereabouts of many others cannot be traced.This is what is called a ‘ghost voter list’,” he said.The remarks followed the BJP-JD(S) alliance's sweep of all four Karnataka legislative council seats, despite Congress being in power in the state. The results also saw Congress lose its sitting Bengaluru Teachers’ constituency to the JD(S), while the BJP retained three seats.PM Modi's reference to ballot papers comes amid the opposition's repeated allegations of irregularities in electronic voting machines (EVMs) and demands for greater transparency in the electoral process.
Article Summary: Mallikarjun Kharge says opposition will not give up its demand for ballot paper voting. He also challenged the BJP to dissolve Parliament and contest elections using ballot papers. Prime Minister Narendra Modi took a dig at Congress for "drawing a blank" in recent MLC elections.

Article Title: 'Cancel passport, Aadhaar, block social media account': PIL seeks action against CJP spokesperson Saurav Das; Madras HC seeks Centre, X and Instagram's response within 6 weeks
Article Text:
CJP spokesperson Saurav Das





CHENNAI: A PIL has been filed in the Madras high court seeking an inquiry into the antecedents of Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) spokesperson and journalist Saurav Das . The petition also seeks the blocking of his social media accounts over alleged derogatory remarks against the judiciary.Admitting the petition, a first bench comprising Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G Arul Murugan directed the Union home ministry, the ministry of external affairs, the ministry of law and justice, and the grievance officers of X and Instagram to respond within six weeks.The petition, filed by Ganesh Kumar, has sought directions to the government to conduct a detailed and fair inquiry into Saurav Das's background and take action, including the cancellation of his passport and Aadhaar card. It also seeks directions to the authorities to block his social media accounts to prevent him from making allegedly derogatory remarks against the judiciary.The petitioner alleged that despite submitting a representation seeking action against Saurav Das, the authorities had failed to act, prompting him to approach the court.
Article Summary: A PIL has been filed in the Madras high court seeking an inquiry into the antecedents of Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) spokesperson Saurav Das. The petition also seeks the blocking of his social media accounts over alleged derogatory remarks against the judiciary.

Article Title: Judge named accused in son’s fatal Mercedes crash gets interim protection from arrest
Article Text:
Jayabalakrishnan, who ran a roadside eatery, was heading home after closing the shop when the accident occurred at 2.20 am on Sunday. Both vehicles were travelling towards Kalamassery.





KOCHI: The Kerala high court on Thursday granted interim protection from arrest to the additional district judge whose 17-year-old son allegedly drove a Mercedes-Benz that hit a two-wheeler in Kochi, killing the rider.Justice Kauser Edappagath passed the order on an anticipatory bail plea filed by the judge, who is posted at a Motor Accident Claims Tribunal in Irinjalakuda, Thrissur district.“The police shall not arrest the applicant until further orders. However, he shall appear before the investigating officer today at 1pm and if necessary as and when called for. The interrogation of the applicant shall be done in accordance with the guidelines laid down by the Supreme Court,” the court ordered.Senior advocate P Vijaya Bhanu, appearing for the judge, told the court that his client had appeared before the police on Wednesday and was interrogated for more than four hours. Another notice directing him to appear before the police had since been issued.According to Bar and Bench, questioning the need for further interrogation and custodial questioning, the court remarked, “What was the need to interrogate him for four hours and now for further interrogation? Why is his arrest required? He is a judicial officer.He will co-operate with the investigation.”Counsel representing the victim’s legal heirs opposed the plea, alleging that the judge had tampered with evidence after being informed of the accident.The court said it had to proceed strictly in accordance with the law and granted interim protection from arrest. It also asked the prosecutor to provide the state’s response to the plea.The judge was named as an accused in the FIR registered after the October 25 crash in Cheranalloor, Kochi, in which his minor son allegedly drove the car that hit a two-wheeler, killing Jayabalakrishnan.In his anticipatory bail plea, the judge claimed he had no knowledge that the vehicle had been taken from the premises. He said he learnt of the accident after receiving a phone call while asleep.The plea also argued that Section 105 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, which deals with culpable homicide not amounting to murder, requires knowledge that the act is likely to cause death.Meanwhile, the victim’s family has complained to the Kerala high court chief justice seeking an inquiry into the judicial officer’s conduct. According to Bar & Bench, the High Court’s Administrative Committee held a preliminary meeting on October 27 and decided to await further material from the investigating agency before taking any action against the judge.
Article Summary: The Kerala high court on Thursday granted interim protection from arrest to the additional district judge. His 17-year-old son allegedly drove a Mercedes-Benz that hit a two-wheeler in Kochi, killing the rider. Justice Kauser Edappagath passed the order on an anticipatory bail plea filed by the judge, who is posted at a Motor Accident Claims Tribunal.

Article Title: Rs 1 lakh bribe trap: Navi Mumbai ACB catches circle officer, talathi and woman assistant
Article Text:
The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite, Jaihind Birsha Koli (49) and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36).





NAVI MUMBAI: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe from a villager in Chirner, Uran taluka, to register the names of his relatives in the 7/12 extract of a land record.The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36), an assistant to the revenue officials.Dharmaraj Sonake, deputy superintendent of police, Navi Mumbai ACB, said the complainant had applied to register the names of the heirs of his deceased sister in the 7/12 extract of their land in Chirner.The land was jointly owned by the complainant's maternal uncle, aunt, brother and sister. The complainant had also applied for deletion of his deceased brother's name and submitted the request to circle officer Mohite and talathi Koli. However, the two officials allegedly demanded Rs 1 lakh from him to process the work.Dy SP Sonake said, "After verification of the complaint on Monday, when it was confirmed that the revenue officers Mohite and Koli had told the complainant to hand over the bribe amount to the accused woman assistant Monika Patil, a trap was laid on Tuesday around 2 pm. After the woman assistant Monika Patil accepted the demanded bribe of Rs 1 lakh from the complainant and handed it over to circle officer Keshav Mohite, both were caught red-handed and arrested. While, the acccused Talathi Jaihind Koli who was involved in the bribe demand was taken into custody from Dronagiri."
Article Summary: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe. The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36)

Article Title: Man in Mahindra Thar with duplicate plate molests woman, knocks down another in Kharghar
Article Text:
30-year-old man was apprehended for allegedly molesting a woman and injuring another in Navi Mumbai.





NAVI MUMBAI: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team within 10 hours on Thursday evening.He had allegedly molested a 26-year-old woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night and, an hour later, severely injured a 22-year-old woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, Kharghar.Acting on a complaint by the woman allegedly molested by the Thar SUV driver, Kharghar police registered an FIR under BNS section 74 for the offence of assault or criminal force against a woman with the intent to outrage her modesty.While, as per the complaint by the injured woman Shrawani Dandekar, a resident of sector 3, Belpada, an FIR under relevant BNS sections and Motor Vehicle Act was registered against the Thar SUV driver for rash and negligent driving causing hurt.The detained aaccused identified as Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of sector 50, Seawoods, Nerul was handed over to Kharghar police for further legal action.Previously, in January 2021, he was arrested by Nerul police in the FIR registered against him for alleged kidnapping, sexual harassment and molestation of a woman.Sanjay Joshi, senior inspector of Kharghar said, "The accused Nakhvi has been detained and subsequently it will be decided whether to arrest him or serve with a notice under Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) for cooperating in police investigating."Audumbar Patil, senior inspector of crime branch unit-3 said, "After an FIR for molestation was registered at Kharghar police station by the victim woman, a resident of sector 34, Kharghar. As per the orders of higher authority, our team started a parallel probe. From the CCTV camera surveillance near the crime scene, we obtained the red Thar SUV's registration number, which was of Vashi RTO passing.""When verified, the registration number was found to be that of a Maruti WagonR car. As the accused had used a duplicate registration number plate, we scrutinized as many as 62 Thar SUVs registered with various Regional Transport Offices (RTOs). Subsequently, we obtained the registration number of a red Thar SUV that was registered with Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar RTO," Patil added.SPI Patil further informed, "The SUV was registered in the name of Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of Devaki Apartment in sector-50, Seawoods. From his mobile number registered with the RTO, his location was tracked.""He was apprehended from Bonkode village, Koparkhairane on Thursday late evening. Upon thorough interrogation, he confessed that he had inappropriately touched the woman pedestrian near Pethpada metro station while he drove his Thar SUV and sped away. He even confessed to have injured a woman pedestrian by hitting her his SUV while driving in Belpada area," he said.
Article Summary: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team on Thursday evening. He had allegedly molested a woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night. An hour later, he severely injured a woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, KharGHar.

NAVI MUMBAI: In a major security lapse at Belapur Railway Protection Force (RPF), two women arrested for allegedly attempting to steal overhead electric wires from the Juinagar railway godown escaped from the lockup after midnight on September 28.One of them was apprehended around six hours later, while the other remains at large.The woman constable on night duty has been suspended and a departmental inquiry has been initiated against her.As per the FIR registered by RPF sub-inspector Milap Parte (52) at Panvel GRP, a case was registered on September 24 under Section 3(a) of the Railway Property (Unauthorized Possession) Act, 1966, Amendment 2012, at Belapur railway police station.The case was based on a written memo submitted by RPF personnel Ravikant Gade regarding the theft of overhead electric wires from the godown at Juinagar railway station on September 21.During the probe, a trap was laid on September 26 and around 1pm, two women were found loitering suspiciously near the Juinagar godown with the alleged intention of committing theft.They were taken into custody and identified as Rupali Kailas Kurhade (30), from Jalna, and Shalibai Ashok Pawar (49), from Bhiwandi.They were arrested after an FIR was registered for attempted theft and produced before a CSMT court, which remanded them to police custody till September 30. They were lodged in the lockup at Belapur RPF police station.Day-shift woman constable Rakhi Malaiya was assigned guard duty at the lockup, after which woman head constable Pooja Bagre was on night duty.Around 2am on September 28, when Bagre had gone to the toilet, the two women allegedly managed to open the lock by inserting their hands through the iron bars of the lockup and jerking it. Police suspect the lock may not have been secured properly.The women then reached the balcony at the rear end of the police station. They removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping.The incident was captured on CCTV footage. PSI Parte learnt about the escape after waking up at home around 6.30am and finding several missed calls from head constable Bagre and ASI Rajiv Parsan.Sunil Nila, chief spokesperson of Central Railway, said, "One accused woman Rupali Kurhade was apprehended from near Nerul railway station around 8.45 am. The other accused Shalibai Pawar is still absconding."
Article Summary: The women removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping. One of them was apprehended around six hours later, while the other remains at large. The woman constable on night duty has been suspended and a departmental inquiry has been initiated.

Article Title: TMC suspends fire chief over immersion ghats lapses
Article Text:
Thane municipal corporation





THANE: The Thane municipal corporation (TMC) on Friday suspended its acting chief fire officer (CFO) over alleged negligence in providing adequate safety equipment at idol immersion ghats on Oct 20. Action has also been taken against two other officials, while show-cause notices have been served on two junior staff, it is learnt.The suspension order is issued by additional municipal commissioner-1, Prashant Rode, holds Jhalke responsible for lapses in carrying out his duties. The order states that he has been suspended under the Maharashtra Civil Services (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1979. Jhalke, who is the fire officer and in-charge of Balkum fire station, has been handling the additional charge of CFO for the last several years."Certain safety arrangements at Datta Mandir Ghat and Ahilyadevi Ghat at Masunda Lake were allegedly found to be inadequate, with a particular shortfall in life jackets and other essential safety equipment. The shortcomings were apparently pointed out to deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde who also expressed concern at the alleged negligence," said a civic official.Officials said that during the suspension period, Jhalke will be required to comply with the prescribed conditions and cannot take up other employment or engage in business without the requisite permission.
Article Summary: Thane municipal corporation suspends acting chief fire officer (CFO) over alleged negligence. Action also taken against two other officials, while show- cause notices have been served on two junior staff. Safety arrangements at Datta Mandir Ghat and Ahilyadevi Ghat at Masunda Lake allegedly found to be inadequate.

Article Title: Sealed Thane flat in Iqbal Kaskar-Dawood Ibrahim money laundering case breached; ED reclaims property, files FIR
Article Text:
Thane flat linked to Iqbal Kaskar’s extortion case targeted for occupation





MUMBAI: Enforcement Directorate (ED) filed an FIR for trespassing and attempting to occupy a flat in Thane which was attached in a money laundering case it investigated against Iqbal Kaskar and his Pakistan-based gangster brother Dawood Ibrahim The flat was attached in the case in 2022, in the money laundering case linked to extortion by Iqbal Kaskar and others.The flat was in ED’s possession and it had put its seal on the lock. Kaskar had acquired the flat through extortion and threat in 2015 and got it registered in the name of his associate Mumtaz Azaz Sheikh, alias Raju.Recently, the ED learnt that certain persons entered the flat after removing its possession notice, claiming ownership of the flat.Since the money laundering case is pending in the court, the ED informed the court about it, repossessed the flat and filed a police case last week.
Article Summary: Enforcement Directorate (ED) filed an FIR for trespassing and attempting to occupy a flat in Thane. The flat was attached in a money laundering case it investigated against Iqbal Kaskar and his Pakistan-based gangster brother Dawood Ibrahim. The ED repossessed the flat and filed a police case last week.

Article Title: ACB registers case against Pimpri Chinchwad Municipal Corporation senior official for allegedly seeking bribe to sign tender agreements of water supply dept worth Rs 91.57 lakh
Article Text:
Pune:





The Pune division’s Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has registered a case against Pimpri Chinchwad Municipal Corporation senior official for allegedly demanding a bribe from a contractor to sign agreements for five water supply department tenders worth Rs 91.57 lakh.According to ACB officials, the contractor was awarded five works related to maintenance, repairs and the laying of new pipelines. He was required to sign agreements with the civic body to obtain work orders and had been following up with officials to complete the formalities.The contractor alleged that officials demanded a bribe of 0.5% of the tender value to clear the agreements. Following verification of the complaint, the ACB found that a senior official had allegedly demanded Rs 19,000, calculated at 0.5% of the Rs 38 lakh value of three tender files pending with him.A senior ACB official said the PCMC official had also admitted to accepting a similar bribe from the contractor earlier. A case was registered against him under the Prevention of Corruption Act at Sant Tukaram Nagar police station, and he was taken into custody for investigation.Shirish Sardeshpande, superintendent of the ACB’s Pune division, said even demanding a bribe was an offence and urged citizens to report such incidents through the bureau’s WhatsApp helpline or contact numbers.
Article Summary: The Pune division’s Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has registered a case against Pimpri Chinchwad Municipal Corporation senior official. The contractor was awarded five works related to maintenance, repairs and the laying of new pipelines. He had been following up with officials to complete the formalities.

Article Title: Malegaon civic chief among 3 arrested for Rs 80,000 bribe demand
Article Text:
Nashik:





The anti-corruption bureau on Thursday arrested Malegaon’s municipal commissioner Ravindra Jadhav, his personal assistant Nilesh Patil and accountant Harish Dimber for allegedly demanding a bribe of Rs 80,000 to clear payments for civic works. The arrests came just days before Jadhav’s retirement on Oct 31.According to the anti-corruption bureau (ACB), the trio demanded 4% commission from the complainant who had been authorised by two contractors to realise the payments from the civic body.“The complainant had submitted a formal complaint on July 9, 2026, stating that authorisation letters were issued for two contractors who executed municipal works for the Malegaon Municipal Corporation. To disburse the bills directly to the contractors’ bank accounts via RTGS, the public servants demanded a 4% bribe on each of the two bills, totalling Rs 80,000. Following the verification of the demand, a trap was laid by the ACB on Thursday and the three were arrested,” said deputy superintendent of police (ACB) Swatee Pawar.Police said Patil repeatedly demanded the bribe on July 10 and 13 and assured the complainant that he would consult the commissioner.The ACB further alleged that Jadhav himself reiterated the demand on July 24 and indicated that the money could be collected after the contractors received their payments. Officials said Dimber allegedly supported and facilitated the demand during subsequent interactions.Based on the complaint and verification of the demand, the ACB laid a trap on Thursday. Jadhav and Patil were arrested in Igatpuri while travelling towards Mumbai, while Dimber was held in Malegaon. A case has been registered at Malegaon Killa police station under the Prevention of Corruption Act. Jadhav has been booked under section 7, while Patil and Dimber face charges under sections 7 and 12.ACB teams also carried out searches at the residences and premises linked to the accused and are examining documents that could strengthen the investigation.Malegaon’s deputy mayor Shaan-e-Hind Nihal Ahmed called for administrative reforms in the civic body. “While the law will decide the fate in this case, residents of Malegaon, however, hope that govt will now depute IAS officers as commissioners, as they are better administrators and are dedicated for the development of the local bodies,” Ahmed said.
Article Summary: Malegaon’s municipal commissioner Ravindra Jadhav, his personal assistant Nilesh Patil and accountant Harish Dimber were arrested on Thursday. The trio demanded 4% commission from the complainant who had been authorised by two contractors to realise the payments from the civic body.

Article Title: 864 bottles of liquor seized from house near Erode; man arrested
Article Text: ERODE: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district in the early hours of Thursday and arrested a man.Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid at the house of K Govindaraj, 28, of Ammapalayam. They found 864 bottles of IMFL stocked in the house for illegal sale.Police registered a case and arrested Govindaraj. He was remanded in judicial custody.They launched a search for Sekar alias Ammasai, 34, and Sridhar, 38, who have links with the illegal liquor operation.
Article Summary: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district. Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid.

Article Title: TVK functionary held for sexually harassing student after offering lift
Article Text:
Madurai:





A Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) functionary, who sexually harassed a college student after offering her a lift in his car while she waited for a bus in the rain, was arrested on Thursday after remaining absconding for more than a week. He was apprehended at Maruthancode near Thuckalay.The accused, L Christopher, 40, from Marunthu Kottai near Thuckalay, was a member of TVK’s Kanyakumari central district executive committee. He was removed from the party following the complaint.According to police, the complainant, a postgraduate student from a private college in Nagercoil, regularly travelled with another student from Moolachal, who was also a TVK functionary.On October 21, the two students were waiting for a bus after college when it began raining. Christopher, who knew the other student, stopped his car and offered them a lift, saying he was travelling in the same direction.After dropping the TVK member at Moolachel, Christopher continued towards Kulasekaram with the complainant, assuring her that he would drop her near her residence.“The student alleged that Christopher stopped the car midway and sexually harassed her.She confronted him and attempted to get out of the vehicle. He subsequently dropped her near her home and fled,” an investigating officer said.The student informed her parents and subsequently approached police with her friend.Following allegations that police initially failed to register her complaint at Kottrikodu police station, Kanyakumari SP Anshul Nagar ordered an inquiry. Thuckalay police subsequently registered a case against Christopher.Women’s organisations had held a protest in Thuckalay on Monday demanding his arrest.
Article Summary: A Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) functionary sexually harassed a college student after offering her a lift in his car while she waited for a bus in the rain. L Christopher, 40, was a member of TVK’s Kanyakumari central district executive committee.

Article Title: Woman hacked to death, gold chain snatched in Tuticorin
Article Text: Tuticorin: A 45-year-old woman was hacked to death allegedly by her 29-year-old nephew who entered her house on Wednesday afternoon and escaped with her four-sovereign gold thali chain.Police identified the deceased as C Sasikala, wife of Chithiraivel, a native of Third Mile area. Chithiraivel has been working in Kerala, while Sasikala was living alone at the house. Their married son lives separately and their daughter resides in Chennai.According to police, the incident occurred around 2.30 pm when the man, K Vignesh, entered the house and attacked Sasikala with a sickle, inflicting multiple cut injuries. He then fled with her thali chain.Thenpagam police rushed to the spot and sent the body to Tuticorin Govt Medical College Hospital for postmortem examination. Police launched an investigation and secured Vignesh. Initial investigation suggested that it was a murder for gain.
Article Summary: Police identified the deceased as C Sasikala, wife of Chithiraivel, a native of Third Mile area. Their married son lives separately and their daughter resides in Chennai. Police launched an investigation and secured Vignesh. Initial investigation suggested that it was a murder for gain.

Article Title: Sub-inspector suspended for bid to make minor girl retract Pocso complaint against her father
Article Text: MADURAI: A police sub-inspector in Ramanathapuram district tried to pressure a minor girl into withdrawing a Pocso complaint against her father, asking her to deny the sexual abuse allegations to help him secure bail.Following an inquiry, superintendent of police G Chandeesh has ordered the SI’s suspension.The girl’s father was arrested last month under Pocso Act for allegedly sexually abusing her.He was subsequently remanded to judicial custody.A senior police officer said the uncle of the accused was attempting to secure his release on bail when he approached Asaikumar, a sub-inspector attached to the Thondi police station who was handling court-related duties. “Asaikumar demanded and accepted a bribe, promising to help secure bail if the relative followed his instructions,” said the officer.The girl’s family approached the SP with an audio recording of the SI allegedly instructing the uncle of the accused to make the girl claim that she had made a false allegation and no sexual abuse had taken place. The complaint prompted a departmental inquiry which substantiated the allegations against the SI.
Article Summary: The girl’s father was arrested last month under Pocso Act for allegedly sexually abusing her. He was subsequently remanded to judicial custody. The uncle of the accused was attempting to secure his release on bail when he approached Asaikumar, a sub-inspector attached to the Thondi police station.

Article Title: PE teacher suspended after national flag turns upside down at state sports meet in Salem
Article Text: SALEM: A physical education teacher has been suspended following a protocol lapse during the opening ceremony of the state-level 67th Republic Day Athletics Competitions held at the Mahatma Gandhi Sports Ground here on Wednesday.The incident occurred when the state transport minister A Vijay Tamilan Parthiban was hoisting the national flag, and a snag in the rope caused the flag to fly upside down. The event was organized by the state school education department.Taking immediate note of the negligence during the flag-hoisting ceremony, Salem chief educational officer A Ellappan issued an order placing physical education teacher John Jamindar who had supervised the flag hoisting area.
Article Summary: A physical education teacher has been suspended following a protocol lapse during the opening ceremony of the state-level 67th Republic Day Athletics Competitions. The incident occurred when the state transport minister A Vijay Tamilan Parthiban was hoisting the national flag. A snag in the rope caused the flag to fly upside down.

Article Title: Two history-sheeters who escaped from Attayampatti police station nabbed
Article Text: SALEM: Two history-sheeters, who escaped from the Attayampatti police station in Salem district on Tuesday, were nabbed in the early hours of Wednesday.The duo, identified as Santhosh Kumar and Prabhu, are residents of Kandarkula Manickam near Attayampatti. According to police, Santhosh Kumar and Prabhu were brought to the Attayampatti police station on Tuesday morning in connection with robbery and theft cases and questioned by sub-inspector Krishnan and other police personnel. Subsequently, cases were registered against them.Later, police were making arrangements to produce them before a court in the evening. “However, taking advantage of an opportunity, Santhosh Kumar and Prabhu managed to escape from the police station,” said a police officer.Special police teams were formed to trace them. After an intensive search operation, the duo were tracked down and arrested from near Tiruchengode around 3am on Wednesday.They were brought back to the Attayampatti police station for further inquiry. Later, they were lodged in the Salem Central Prison under judicial custody.
Article Summary: The duo, identified as Santhosh Kumar and Prabhu, are residents of Kandarkula Manickam near Attayampatti. They were brought to the police station on Tuesday morning in connection with robbery and theft cases and questioned by sub- inspector Krishnan and other police personnel.

Article Title: SI arrested for stealing MDMA seized in narcotics case from station
Article Text:
Kochi

:





Ernakulam Central Police on Thursday arrested a sub-inspector attached to the same police station for allegedly stealing MDMA seized by police in a narcotics case.The arrested person is Aneez S Thoufeeq, 29, a native of Thiruvananthapuram. Earlier in the day, he was suspended based on a special branch report.As per the FIR, the officer acted with the intention of stealing the contraband in police custody. The FIR was registered on the complaint of an officer who was in charge of the strong room of the station. Drugs which were seized in various narcotics cases were stored in the strong room ahead of moving them to the godown at the DHQ camp for disposal. The difference inAccording to the FIR, Thoufeeq entered the strong room without permission and allegedly stole a sealed packet which contained 87.37g of MDMA seized by Elamakkara Police in a narcotics case on Oct 18. He then tampered with the evidence, knowing that it was MDMA. The action of the accused resulted in a difference in the quantity of MDMA contained in it.As per the suspension order against the officer, officers later noticed a discrepancy in the quantity of the drug. After learning that an inquiry was under way, he allegedly returned another unsealed packet containing 202g of MDMA on Oct 26.The police registered the FIR under Sections 306 (theft by clerk or servant of property in possession of master) and 238 (causing disappearance of evidence) of BNS and Section 21(c) (punishment for offences involving a commercial quantity of manufactured drugs) of the NDPS Act.The police said that an investigation is under way into the motive behind the officer’s action. They have also launched a probe into the financial background of the officer. They are also checking whether he received assistance from anyone else at the station.Incidentally, Thoufeeq was involved in creating awareness against drugs under Operation Toofan.
Article Summary: The arrested person is Aneez S Thoufeeq, 29, a native of Thiruvananthapuram. Earlier in the day, he was suspended based on a special branch report. As per the FIR, the officer acted with the intention of stealing the contraband in police custody.
